speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me understand your condition, could you tell me when these symptoms started and if you have experienced any fever or shortness of breath?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Spontaneous Esophageal Rupture).

The combination of forceful retching following heavy alcohol consumption, immediate onset of severe chest pain, and the patient's inability to communicate due to choking strongly suggests an esophageal rupture. Please prepare the patient for an urgent CT scan of the chest with oral contrast to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_With_Oral_Contrast
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CXR
